chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela and Mansur ibn Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no eye that does not weep on the Day of Judgment, except for an eye that wept from the fear of Allah; and no eye that overflowed with its tears out of the dread of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would prohibit the rest of his body from the Fire; nor would it overflow upon his cheek, so that face would not be covered with darkness or humiliation. And there is nothing that does not have a measure and a weight, except for the tear, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would extinguish oceans of Fire with a little of it. So if a servant were to weep in a community, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would be Merciful to that community because of the weeping of that servant.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and protection of weeping from fear of God in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the weeping of regret and the superior merit of tears shed from khawf (awe/fear) of Allah, a state highly valued by the Imams as a sign of sincere faith. It underscores the metaphysical weight of tears, noting that unlike other deeds which have measured limits, divine mercy for a single tear is boundless, capable of extinguishing oceans of Hellfire. This concept reinforces the Shia emphasis on internal spiritual states manifesting through physical acts of devotion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela and Mansour Bin Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from an eye except that it would be weeping on the Day of Judgment except for the eye which wept from fear of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>; and there is no eye which overflows with its tears out of fear of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic except that Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Prohibit the rest of his body upon the Fire; nor would it overflow upon his cheek, that face would neither wear out not be disgraced; and there is none from the things except for it is a measurement and a weight except for the tears, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Extinguish oceans of Fire by a little of it. So if a servant were to weep in a community, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be Merciful to that community due to the weeping of that servant (from fear of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah and Mansur ibn Yunus from Muhammad ibn Marwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Judgment except the eye that has wept for fear of Allah. Any eye that is flooded with tears for fear of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, will make it forbidden for the fire to burn the other parts of his body. Any eye from which tears flow over one’s checks such face will not face any suffering or humiliation. Everything has weighing and measuring tools except tears with a very little of which Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will extinguish oceans of fire. If a servant (of Allah) weeps in a nation, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will grant favor to that nation because of the weeping of that one servant (of Allah).”
